Fit one logistic regression per feature of a 0/1 table, such as a detection table

stats_fit_logistic.Rd

Fit one logistic regression per feature of a 0/1 feature-by-sample table, such as a detection table, and test each named coefficient with a Wald z.

mzLib's LogisticRegression.Fit models logit P(outcome = 1) = X beta for every feature (row) separately, by maximum likelihood, and tests each coefficient with a two-sided Wald z. It is R's glm(y ~ 0 + X, family = binomial) per feature, which mzLib reproduces to 1e-8 relative in the coefficients (1e-6 in standard errors and p-values).

Usage

stats_fit_logistic(responses, design, coefficients, max_iterations = NULL,
  tolerance = NULL, threads = 1, timeout = 600)

Arguments

responses

A TSV with a header row: the feature id first, then one column per sample, named by its header - stats_fit's layout - with every cell 0, 1, or blank / NA / NaN for missing (left out of that feature's fit). Any other value is refused.

design

stats_fit's design: a TSV with a header row and one row per sample, the sample name (matching the responses header, in any order) then one numeric column per coefficient. Include an intercept column yourself if you want one.

coefficients

Design column names to report, each as one block of rows. Every design column is fitted whatever you name.

max_iterations

The IRLS iteration limit per feature (iterations). Leave it NULL for mzLib's default (100 at mzLib d10017ce); a feature still changing at the limit is "not_converged".

tolerance

Stop when the relative change in deviance is below this (R glm()'s rule). Leave it NULL for mzLib's default (1e-12 at mzLib d10017ce), which is tighter than glm()'s 1e-8.

threads

Features fitted at once (threads), or -1 for every core. The answer is identical at any value.

timeout

Seconds to allow, or NULL to wait indefinitely.

Details

The usual question in proteomics: is a feature's chance of being measured related to the condition? Write 1 where a protein was quantified and 0 where it was not; a coefficient far from 0 says its missing values are not missing at random.

A feature is reported - never dropped - when it cannot be fitted. "separated" is the one to read carefully: the design splits its 0s from its 1s (or every outcome is the same), so no finite estimate exists. R's glm() prints a huge coefficient and a warning there; mzLib reports the status and NA. Look at events and observed for those rows.

Value

An mzlibr_logistic_model_fit:

- records, a data.frame with one row per (reported coefficient, feature) - one block of feature_count rows per coefficient you named, in that order, each in the responses file's feature order: feature; coefficient; status; estimate, the maximum-likelihood coefficient in log-odds per coefficient unit, so exp(estimate) is the odds ratio; standard_error (log-odds per coefficient unit), from the inverse Fisher information at the estimate; z (standard errors), the Wald statistic; p_value, a fraction (0 to 1), two-sided and not adjusted across features; deviance (deviance, -2 log L), the feature's residual deviance; iterations, IRLS iterations used (0 when no fit was attempted); observed, samples with a 0 or 1; and events, observed samples whose outcome is 1. Statistics are NA where status is not "fitted". - responses_file and design_file, as absolute paths; feature_count features and sample_count samples read; sample_names; coefficient_names (every design column) and tested_coefficients; max_iterations (iterations) and tolerance (relative change in deviance) as you passed them, NA when left to mzLib; threads; missing_count response cells (cells); status_counts, features per status; row_count rows; column_names. - caveats: what the numbers are and are not, with a count of unfitted features by status.

What it is not

Wald tests are the least reliable of the likelihood tests near separation and in small samples; no likelihood-ratio test is offered, and Firth's penalized likelihood (logistf), which gives finite estimates for separated features, is not implemented. Send one coefficient's p_value column to stats_adjust for Benjamini-Hochberg.

Wraps

Wire verb stats fit-logistic. Generated from the bridge's verb spec stats.fit-logistic.yaml (bridge commit aea14604d5f7) by scripts/build-man.R; the spec owns these facts, and all three bindings render the same ones.

  • LogisticRegression.Fit in mzLib/StatisticalModels/LogisticRegression.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • LogisticModelFit in mzLib/StatisticalModels/LogisticRegression.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • LogisticRegression.SeparationThreshold in mzLib/StatisticalModels/LogisticRegression.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • FeatureFitStatus in mzLib/StatisticalModels/LinearModel.cs at mzLib d10017ce

Parameters: units, ranges and defaults

responses

path; required. stats fit's responses table, with outcomes for cells. A TSV with a header row: the first column is the feature id (unique, any header) and every other column is one sample, named by its header. Every cell is 0, 1, or blank, NA or NaN (any case) for missing, which is omitted from that feature's fit. mzLib refuses any other value (a proportion is not a binary outcome); the refusal names the feature and sample. A 0 is an outcome, not a missing value. Blank lines are skipped.

design

path; required. stats fit's design table. A TSV with a header row and one row per sample: the sample name, matching the responses header exactly (rows are matched by name, in any order), then one column per coefficient, every cell a finite number. Used as written: include an intercept column if you want one. mzLib refuses a design that is not of full column rank over all samples.

coefficients (wire --stdin)

string[]; required; range >= 1 line; each a design column name, none repeated. The coefficients to report, one design column name per line. The model always fits every design column; the table holds one block of rows per coefficient named here, in this order.

max_iterations (wire --max-iterations)

int; in iterations; default absent; range >= 1 (mzLib's rule; anything else is mzLib's refusal, a usage error). The iteratively reweighted least squares iteration limit per feature (LogisticRegression.Fit maxIterations). A feature still changing at the limit is not_converged. Absent, the bridge sends none and mzLib's default applies (100 at d10017ce), and the envelope's max_iterations is null.

tolerance

float; in relative change in deviance (unitless); default absent; range > 0 (mzLib's rule; anything else is mzLib's refusal, a usage error). Convergence rule (LogisticRegression.Fit tolerance): iteration stops when |dev - dev_prev| / (|dev| + 0.1) is below it, R glm's rule. Absent, the bridge sends none and mzLib's default applies (1e-12 at d10017ce, tighter than glm's default epsilon of 1e-8), and the envelope's tolerance is null.

threads

int; in threads; default 1; range >= 1, or -1 for every core. Features fitted at once. The bridge default is 1 (BULK.md); mzLib's own default is -1. Results are identical at any value (mzLib).

Returned fields

Each field with its type, its unit, and what NA means when it is NA.

responses_file

string; never NA. Absolute path of the responses table.

design_file

string; never NA. Absolute path of the design table.

feature_count

int; in features; never NA. Feature rows read.

sample_count

int; in samples; never NA. Sample columns read.

sample_names

string[]; never NA. In responses header order, which is the order the design rows were put in.

coefficient_names

string[]; never NA. Every design column, in order.

tested_coefficients

string[]; never NA. The stdin coefficients, in order; the table holds one block of feature_count rows per entry.

max_iterations

int; in iterations; NA when not given: mzLib's default was used (100 at d10017ce). The iteration limit sent to mzLib.

tolerance

float; in relative change in deviance (unitless); NA when not given: mzLib's default was used (1e-12 at d10017ce). The convergence tolerance sent to mzLib.

threads

int; in threads; never NA. The thread count used.

missing_count

int; in cells; never NA. Response cells that were blank, NA or NaN.

status_counts

map<string,int>; in features; never NA. Features per status, always these five keys: fitted, too_few_observations, rank_deficient, separated, not_converged. They are the outcomes LogisticRegression.Fit's body can return at d10017ce; a stop-gap until mzLib says per model (mzLib#1487).

row_count

int; in rows; never NA. feature_count x the number of tested coefficients.

column_names

string[]; never NA. The table's columns, in order.

records (wire columns)

table; never NA. One row per (tested coefficient, feature): coefficient blocks in stdin order, features in file order.

caveats

string[]; never NA. Four static caveats, plus one with the counts when any feature was not fitted.

Columns of records

feature

string; never NA. The feature id from the responses file's first column.

coefficient

string; never NA. The coefficient this row reports.

status

string; never NA. fitted | too_few_observations (no more observed samples than coefficients) | rank_deficient (the design restricted to the observed samples is not of full rank) | separated (the observed outcomes are all 0, all 1, or split by the design, so no finite maximum-likelihood estimate exists; mzLib calls a fit separated when a fitted probability comes within LogisticRegression.SeparationThreshold, 1e-10 at d10017ce, of 0 or 1) | not_converged (still changing at max-iterations). Only fitted rows carry statistics.

estimate

float; in log-odds per coefficient unit (the log odds ratio for a 0/1 column); NA when status is not fitted. The maximum-likelihood coefficient on the logit scale. exp(estimate) is the odds ratio.

standard_error

float; in log-odds per coefficient unit; NA when not fitted. From the inverse Fisher information at the estimate.

z

float; in standard errors; NA when not fitted. Wald statistic, estimate / standard_error.

p_value

float; in fraction (0 to 1); NA when not fitted. Two-sided Wald p-value against a coefficient of 0, from the standard normal. Not adjusted across features.

deviance

float; in deviance (-2 x log-likelihood, natural log); NA when not fitted. The feature's residual deviance; the same in every coefficient block.

iterations

int; in iterations; never NA. IRLS iterations used. 0 when no fit was attempted (too_few_observations, rank_deficient, or every outcome the same); max-iterations when not_converged; a separated feature that IRLS ran on reports the iterations it ran.

observed

int; in samples; never NA. Samples with a 0 or 1 for this feature.

events

int; in samples; never NA. Observed samples whose outcome is 1.

Errors

Each is an R condition carrying the class shown and mzlib_error; see mzlib_error.

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

responses or design missing, blank or not found; a table empty, header-only or with too few columns; a row whose field count differs from its header; an empty or repeated feature id, sample or coefficient name; a response cell that is not a number (other than blank, NA, NaN); a design cell that is not a finite number; the design's samples are not exactly the responses' sample columns (both differences are named)

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

no coefficient on stdin, one named twice, or one not in the design; --max-iterations or --tolerance without a value or not a number; --threads 0 or below -1

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

mzLib refuses the input (its ArgumentException, reclassified): a response that is not 0, 1 or missing, named by 0-based feature and sample and then by the names in the files; a design not of full column rank; --max-iterations below 1 or --tolerance not above 0

mzlib_bridge_error (correctness)

never expected

mzlib_service_unavailable (service_unavailable)

Never raised by this verb.

Caveats

  • Maximum likelihood by iteratively reweighted least squares, started and stopped as R's glm does; standard errors from the inverse Fisher information at the estimate; Wald z tests. mzLib matches R 4.6.1's glm(family = binomial, epsilon = 1e-14) to 1e-8 relative in coefficients and deviance and to 1e-6 relative in standard errors and p-values (summary.glm takes its weights from the step before the estimate). Wald tests are the least reliable of the likelihood tests near separation and in small samples; no likelihood-ratio test is offered.

  • separated features carry no statistics. R's glm reports large, meaningless coefficients and a warning for them instead. A separated feature can be the strongest effect in the table (detected in every run of one condition and in none of another): read its events and observed counts. Firth's penalized likelihood (logistf), which gives finite estimates there, is not implemented.

  • p_value is not adjusted across features. Send one coefficient's p_value column to stats adjust for Benjamini-Hochberg.

  • A 0 is an outcome (for a detection table: measured as absent), not a missing value. Missing cells are omitted per feature, never imputed.

Performance

Every call starts one bridge process, which costs a .NET start-up before any work.

Same verb in other bindings

  • Python (pyMzLib): pymzlib.stats.fit_logistic

  • Rust (mzLibRust): mzlib::stats::fit_logistic_with with FitLogisticOptions

  • R (mzLibR): stats_fit_logistic

Since

Wire protocol 1; pyMzLib 0.6.0; mzLibRust 0.1.0; mzLibR 0.1.0.

References

  • doi:10.2307/2344614: generalized linear models and their fitting by iteratively reweighted least squares, the estimator mzLib implements (Nelder and Wedderburn, J R Stat Soc A 135:370, 1972)

  • doi:10.1093/biomet/71.1.1: separation: when the outcomes are split by the design the maximum-likelihood estimate does not exist, which is the separated status (Albert and Anderson, Biometrika 71:1, 1984)

See also

stats_fit for the intensities themselves, stats_adjust

Examples


# mzLib's own reference input (80 simulated binary features, 40 samples), and R's glm() output
# for it, which this package ships:
data <- system.file("extdata", "stats", package = "mzLibR")
fit <- stats_fit_logistic(file.path(data, "glm_reference_responses.tsv"),
  file.path(data, "glm_reference_design.tsv"), c("Intercept", "x", "grp"))
fit
#> <mzlibr_logistic_model_fit> 80 features x 40 samples, reporting Intercept, x, grp
#>   fitted 76, too_few_observations 0, rank_deficient 0, separated 4, not_converged 0
x <- fit$records[fit$records$coefficient == "x", ]
glm <- read.delim(file.path(data, "glm_reference_fit.tsv"))
fitted <- glm$status == "fitted"
max(abs(x$estimate[fitted] - glm$b1[fitted]) / abs(glm$b1[fitted]))
#> [1] 4.203008e-12
x[1, c("estimate", "p_value", "events", "observed")]
#>     estimate   p_value events observed
#> 81 0.4592209 0.2723941     25       35
